text:
leo: Thinking out loud — we should plan a migration of GPU autoscaling to Karpenter for heterogeneous instance support in us-west-2. Want to handle spot fallback + predictable latency for production inference. Anyone object?
sara: +1, this makes sense. Main concerns: launch latency for big instances and ENI limits in crowded AZs. :thinking_face:
aj: Agree. Also want to avoid noisy neighbor CPU steal on mixed instances. Can we do a staged approach — dev -> canary -> prod?
cheng: Staged is good. For canary maybe limit to non-critical batch workloads first (re-ranking jobs). Keep inference in dedicated pools until we validate latency.
jamal: FYI we saw 2-3m cold start for p4d last time; g5 launches were closer to 40-60s. If Karpenter picks p4 by default we might regress tail p99. Need explicit instance preference + max price for spot.
leo: Good point. Thinking we can provide a provisioner config with ordered instance types + a maxLaunchDelay SLO and prefer g5 for low-latency lanes. Example sketch:```apiVersion: karpenter.sh/v1alpha5
kind: Provisioner
metadata:
  name: gpu-mixed-provisioner
spec:
  requirements:
  - key: "karpenter.k8s.aws/instance-type"
    operator: In
    values: ["g5.12xlarge","g4dn.12xlarge","p4d.24xlarge"]
  ttlSecondsUntilExpired: 259200
  consolidation:
    enabled: true
  provider:
    subnetSelector:
      karpenter.sh/discovery: us-west-2a
    securityGroupSelector:
      kubernetes.io/cluster/redwood: "owned"
```
sara: Nice. Couple of notes: enable consolidation helps cost but watch pod disruption budgets for long-running jobs. Also set taints so inference-critical pods avoid spot instances: `taints: [{key:","value":"spot","effect":"NoSchedule"}]` with tolerations for batch jobs.
maria: Can we get a quick cost model? Rough numbers: g5 ~ $X/hr, p4d ~ $Y/hr (on-demand). If consolidation + spot fallback works we estimate ~15% unit-cost reduction for batch; maybe 5% for inference if we keep most on on-demand. Those are coarse.
aj: Also check ENI trunking limits per AZ + subnet. Last month we hit ENI deficits when we allowed many medium instances in us-west-2b. Might want a provisioner per-AZ with `limits` to avoid exhausting IPs.
cheng: +1 to per-AZ provisioning, and also set `labels` so scheduler can prefer nodes with gpukind=ampere vs ampere-v2, etc. Karpenter's capacity types can be mixed but set `capacityType: [spot, on-demand]` explicitly.
jamal: For rollback — keep cluster-autoscaler running parallel in canary cluster for 24h and compare behaviors. If Karpenter misses any autoscaling predicates we can switch back by flipping node selectors on the deployment.
leo: Plan proposal: Week1 dev validation (create provisioner in dev cluster, run stress tests), Week2 canary for re-rank + batch in staging (observe p99 tail, spot preemptions), Week3 small prod rollout (10% traffic), Week4 full cutover if metrics look good. Fallback plan ready.
sara: Metrics to track: node launch latency, pod scheduling latency, p99 inference latency, eviction/restart rate, IP exhaustion events, cost per token/throughput. Add alert for >5% restart rate from spot preemptions.
maria: I'll run a quick cost sim and post numbers by EOD Wednesday.
deploy-bot: Reminder: create an IaC PR with provisioner manifest in `infra/karpenter/provisioners/` and add canary tag.
leo: Sweet. Who wants to own the canary run? @cheng? :eyes:
cheng: I can own it — will set up a small canary stack and a dashboard with Grafana panels for the metrics Sara listed.
aj: Ping me when you start, I'll run the failure injection (simulate preemptions + AZ failures).
jamal: I'll validate ENI capacity and adjust subnet pools. If any AZ is tight we'll gate that AZ out of the provisioner.
sara: Sounds good. Document decisions in the migration plan doc and let's sync next Tues. :thumbsup:
